title: sou350121/VLA-Handbook
summary: VLA-Handbook is a Chinese, practice-oriented study and interview guide for algorithm engineers entering Vision-Language-Action work in robotics. It narrows the usual CV/NLP interview scope to robotics-specific issues, making it more useful for people preparing to work on embodied AI systems rather than generic perception or language roles.

title: google-deepmind/mujoco_playground
summary: google-deepmind/mujoco_playground provides a GPU-accelerated environment for training robot learning policies in MuJoCo, with an emphasis on workflows that can transfer from simulation to real hardware. It is useful as a practical playground for running large-scale robot learning experiments quickly while keeping sim-to-real considerations close to the training loop.

extra.full_text: An open-source library for GPU-accelerated robot learning and sim-to-real transfer.

title: DravenALG/awesome-vla-wam
summary: DravenALG/awesome-vla-wam is a curated bibliography and resource list for Vision-Language-Action models and World Action Models, collecting research that connects perception, language, planning, and robot action. It is useful as a map of the fast-moving VLA/WAM literature rather than a runnable tool, helping researchers quickly find relevant papers, benchmarks, and related work around embodied AI and robot control.

title: NVIDIA/warp
summary: NVIDIA Warp is a Python framework for writing GPU-accelerated simulation code aimed at robotics, graphics, physics, and machine learning workloads. It lets users author differentiable kernels in Python that compile to fast CUDA code, making it useful for building custom simulators, physics environments, and learning systems that need tight GPU performance without dropping fully into C++/CUDA.

extra.full_text: A Python framework for GPU-accelerated simulation, robotics, and machine learning.

title: RobotControlStack/robot-control-stack
summary: RobotControlStack is a lightweight sim-to-real stack for training and deploying Vision-Language-Action models and reinforcement learning agents without depending on ROS. It provides native MuJoCo Gymnasium wrappers with synchronous execution across several robot platforms, including Franka, UR5e, xArm, SO101, and YAM, making it useful for researchers who want a leaner path from simulation experiments to real robot control.

extra.full_text: A lean, ROS-free sim-to-real framework for training and deploying Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models and RL agents. Native MuJoCo Gymnasium wrappers with synchronous execution for Franka, UR5e, xArm, SO101 and YAM.

title: isaac-sim/IsaacLab-Arena
summary: Isaac Lab - Arena extends NVIDIA Isaac Lab with a composable simulation layer for assembling robot learning tasks across different embodiments, objects, and environments. It is aimed at rapid prototyping and policy evaluation, making it useful when researchers need to generate diverse simulation setups without rebuilding task infrastructure each time.

extra.full_text: Isaac Lab - Arena is a robotics simulation framework that enhances NVIDIA Isaac Lab by providing a composable, scalable system for creating diverse simulation environments and evaluating robot learning policies. The framework enables developers to rapidly prototype and test robotic tasks with various robot embodiments, objects, and environments.

title: ROBOTIS-GIT/cyclo_lab
summary: ROBOTIS-GIT/cyclo_lab collects reinforcement learning and imitation learning tutorials built around ROBOTIS robots, with an emphasis on taking policies from simulation onto physical hardware. It looks most useful as a hands-on Sim2Real learning and deployment resource for researchers or engineers working with ROBOTIS platforms, rather than as a standalone algorithmic contribution.

extra.full_text: This repository provides tutorials for reinforcement learning and imitation learning using ROBOTIS robots, and supports Sim2Real functionality for deploying the learned policies on real robots.

title: Farama-Foundation/Metaworld
summary: MetaWorld is a suite of simulated robotic manipulation environments used to benchmark multi-task and meta-reinforcement-learning algorithms. It gives researchers a standardized set of robot tasks for testing whether agents can learn across tasks and adapt efficiently, making it useful for comparing generalization and transfer in robot learning.

extra.full_text: Collections of robotics environments geared towards benchmarking multi-task and meta reinforcement learning

title: iit-DLSLab/basic-locomotion-isaaclab
summary: An IsaacLab DirectEnv implementation for training basic quadruped locomotion policies across multiple robot platforms. It is aimed at practical locomotion experimentation, including sim-to-sim transfer and sim-to-real deployment pipelines, so it should be useful as a starting point for researchers moving learned gaits from IsaacLab into other simulators or hardware.

extra.full_text: An IsaacLab DirectEnv for basic quadrupedal locomotion tasks, with support for multiple quadruped robots, sim-to-sim, and sim-to-real pipelines

title: flexivrobotics/isaac_sim_ws
summary: Flexiv’s Isaac Sim workspace adds Flexiv robot models to NVIDIA Isaac Sim and lets them be driven through the same interfaces used on hardware: Flexiv Elements Studio or the Flexiv RDK. The useful bit is that simulation can run against the actual force/torque controller from the real robots, making it a practical setup for testing control workflows before moving to physical Flexiv arms.

extra.full_text: Add Flexiv robots to Isaac Sim and control them using Flexiv Elements Studio or Flexiv RDK with the actual force/torque controller used on real robots.

title: RoboVerseOrg/RoboVerse
summary: RoboVerse aims to unify the robot-learning stack around a shared platform, dataset, and benchmark for training and evaluating scalable, generalizable robot policies. It is positioned as infrastructure for comparing methods across broader robot-learning settings rather than isolated task setups, with emphasis on reproducibility and generalization.

extra.full_text: RoboVerse: Towards a Unified Platform, Dataset and Benchmark for Scalable and Generalizable Robot Learning

title: dartsim/dart
summary: DART is a research-focused C++23 physics engine for robotics, animation, and machine learning, with Python bindings for integrating simulations into experiments and tooling. It is aimed at building and studying articulated-body dynamics, making it useful when researchers need a programmable simulator that sits close to robotics and ML workflows rather than a game-oriented engine.

extra.full_text: Research-focused C++23 physics engine for robotics, animation, and machine learning, with Python bindings

title: DeepRoboticsLab/sdk_deploy
summary: DeepRoboticsLab/sdk_deploy provides sim-to-sim and sim-to-real deployment support for Deep Robotics quadrupeds, currently the M20 and Lite3. It is useful for moving robot control policies or simulation-tested behaviors toward hardware through the vendor SDK path, with a focus on deployment rather than training or benchmarking.

extra.full_text: Sim-to-sim and sim-to-real deployment for Deep Robotics Robots, currently supporting M20 and Lite3

title: D-Robotics/hobot_stereonet
summary: Hobot StereoNet is a D-Robotics deep learning model for stereo depth estimation, taking paired left-right images and producing depth maps fast enough for real-time use. It is aimed at robotics and computer vision systems that need dense 3D perception from stereo cameras, where the practical value is accurate depth recovery without relying on heavier sensing hardware.

extra.full_text: Hobot StereoNet is a high-performance, deep learning-based stereo depth estimation algorithm developed by D-Robotics. It processes stereo image pairs to generate accurate depth maps in real-time, enabling 3D perception for robotics and computer vision applications.
